ledger.note: 4800 BCE: the first megalith builders raise their tombs in Brittany and Poitou. "c. 4800 BC: Constructions in Brittany, France (Barnenez) and Poitou (Bougon)"; "The megalithic structures in the northwest of France are believed to be the oldest in Europe"; the Carnac tumuli date "from the mid-5th millennium BC" (Carnac page). Évora's Almendres, "c. 6000 BC ... Possibly", is drawn from the same year for want of a firmer date.

ledger.note: 3000 BCE: the culture layer closes on the Atlantic megalith builders. The tradition itself continues: "c. 3000 BC: first henges in Britain" and Los Millares, "c. 2500 BC... the climax of the megalithic Bell-beaker culture in Iberia", "c. 1200 BC: Last vestiges of the megalithic tradition"; the end year is this dossier's, chosen where the Megalith page's Atlantic entries pass into the Bronze Age cultures, and bridges a silence.

certainty.note: A monument tradition rather than a bounded culture: modern coastal units around dated monuments, every edge soft.

notes: Culture dossier for the brief's "megalith builders of Atlantic Europe", built from the Megalith page's dated list and the Carnac page: a monument tradition, not an archaeological culture, so the shape is modern coastal units around the dated monuments and the end year (3000 BCE) is a choice, not a page date. Disagreements: Carnac alignments c. 4000 BC (Megalith page) vs "probably around 3300 BC, but some may date to as early as 4500 BC" (Carnac page); whether Mesolithic hunters or Neolithic farmers raised the stones is "still debated" on the Carnac page. Malta's temples (from c. 3600 BC) and the Scandinavian megaliths (Funnelbeaker) are not drawn here. Gazetteer: Carnac, Barnenez, Bougon, Newgrange, Alberite are not places; Vannes is missing from the places list.
